ideas.name: Entropy-Guided Head/Segment Budget Arena
ideas.question: Can attention entropy identify rigid vs dynamic heads online, and when is entropy insufficient without decode-conditioned future support?

ideas.name: Reasoning Branch Cache Sharing and Confident Exit
ideas.question: Can semantically similar reasoning branches safely share cache, and can entropy/confidence stop verification early without near-miss contamination?

ideas.why_scale_fits: Runs as symbolic/tensor toy; no large model needed.

ideas.name: Agentic DFS Search Normal Form
ideas.question: Is tree search/backtracking the right tiny task for observing specialized action-trace and failure-trace mechanisms in a small transformer?

ideas.why_scale_fits: Runs as symbolic/tensor toy; no large model needed.

ideas.name: Spatio-Temporal Cache Drift for GUI-like Trajectories
ideas.question: Do spatial subspace roles and temporal redundancy drift enough that one fused saliency map is structurally wrong?

ideas.why_scale_fits: Runs as symbolic/tensor toy; no large model needed.

ideas.falsifier: If kernel variants all behave like low-rank ridge memory on our tasks, keep this only as theory notes.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Runs as symbolic/tensor toy; no large model needed.

ideas.name: Context-Intensive Extraction Compression Stressor
ideas.question: Do compression methods pass needle lookup but fail when the output requires many independent facts from the prompt?

ideas.falsifier: If single-needle and many-fact extraction have identical rankings, the stressor is not adding value.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Runs as symbolic/tensor toy; no large model needed.

ideas.name: Looped Constant-Memory Reasoning Comparator
ideas.question: When does shared/gated loop memory approximate per-loop KV cache, and when does iterative state overwrite destroy search?
ideas.minimum_test: Compare per-loop cache, shared gated cache, attractor-style refinement, and linear/sparse loop variants on pointer chase/state tracking.
ideas.falsifier: If shared memory never beats a fixed sliding cache at same bytes, do not escalate looped models yet.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Runs as symbolic/tensor toy; no large model needed.

ideas.name: Whole-Document vs Per-Document Sharding Analogy
ideas.question: Can systems sharding ideas inspire better cache segmentation for repeated long documents and branch workloads?
ideas.minimum_test: Synthetic segment packing/object layout simulation: whole-doc blocks, per-doc blocks, and mixed shards under reuse and load balance.

ideas.why_scale_fits: Runs as symbolic/tensor toy; no large model needed.

ideas.name: Entropy-Stability Early Exit Calibration

ideas.falsifier: If entropy stability fails on confidence traps too, early exit needs a stronger hidden-state agreement signal.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Runs as symbolic/tensor toy; no large model needed.

ideas.name: Less-Context Stale-Interference Agent Trap v2
ideas.question: Can retaining all history harm a toy agent compared with recent-tool pruning plus summaries?
ideas.minimum_test: Extend Less-context trap with stale facts, tool outputs, and subgoal summaries; compare full history, recency, summary, intent filtering.
ideas.falsifier: If full context never underperforms, the stale interference setup is too weak.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Runs as symbolic/tensor toy; no large model needed.

ideas.name: Sparse Segment Reuse Correction Battery
ideas.question: When repeated non-prefix segments can be reused, how much sparse correction is needed to restore cross-segment interactions?
ideas.minimum_test: Segment reuse simulator with exact prefix, segment cache, sparse-Q correction, and full recompute upper anchor.
ideas.falsifier: If sparse correction cannot beat no-reuse at safe error rates, demote segment-level cache sharing.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Runs as symbolic/tensor toy; no large model needed.

ideas.name: Cache Probe Taxonomy Refactor v2
ideas.question: Can the cube separate probes by role, failure mode, and metric family so priority decisions stop being manual?
ideas.minimum_test: Traceability report plus per-family metric status; classify every new probe as retention, routing, bounded memory, runtime, search, or training-signal.
ideas.falsifier: If reports still cannot surface orphaned P0 sources or stale probe outputs, strengthen schema rather than adding more experiments.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Runs as symbolic/tensor toy; no large model needed.

ideas.name: Express-style streaming coreset wind tunnel

ideas.name: Centaur HPO state-sharing toy

ideas.name: Prefix-contrast rollout allocation
ideas.question: Is rollout budget best spent at roots or at intermediate prefixes with high terminal-outcome contrast?
ideas.minimum_test: Synthetic rollout tree with uniform/root/prefix/oracle budget policies.

ideas.why_scale_fits: Fits generated data and CPU-scale probes; no large model required.

ideas.name: Backbone-first multi-token acceptance
ideas.question: Is the first predicted token special enough that acceleration should never let auxiliary heads compete with the backbone LM head?

ideas.why_scale_fits: Fits generated data and CPU-scale probes; no large model required.

ideas.name: Joint next-k push-forward toy

ideas.why_scale_fits: Fits generated data and CPU-scale probes; no large model required.

ideas.name: Router-prompt coevolution for heterogeneous streams

ideas.why_scale_fits: Fits generated data and CPU-scale probes; no large model required.

ideas.name: Future-behavior probe for search traces

ideas.why_scale_fits: Fits generated data and CPU-scale probes; no large model required.

ideas.name: Local-linear drift tracker

ideas.why_scale_fits: Fits generated data and CPU-scale probes; no large model required.

ideas.name: Target-distribution design toy SFT

ideas.why_scale_fits: Fits generated data and CPU-scale probes; no large model required.

ideas.name: Phase-diagram discipline for probe selection

ideas.name: Residual checkpoints as cache object
ideas.question: When is storing residual checkpoints plus recomputing K/V a better cache object than storing full KV?

ideas.name: Action-surprise gated writes
ideas.question: Can a write gate based on action/value surprise preserve useful memory with far fewer writes than periodic policies?

ideas.name: Latency-aware lossless block residency

ideas.name: Entropy quench as pre-cache compression
ideas.question: Can token-stream compression remove enough redundancy before KV/cache machinery to change the cache problem?

ideas.why_scale_fits: String/token stream simulators are cheap.

ideas.name: Decoupled erase/write fast-weight memory
ideas.question: Is tying erase and write gates a real failure mode in tiny associative memory, or does decoupling require learned gates to help?

ideas.name: Exact/kernel linear-attention dilution probe
ideas.question: Which kernel constraints actually prevent token-attention dilution in content-addressed recall?

ideas.why_scale_fits: Can be pure tensor/C++ without training.

ideas.why_scale_fits: Audit/refactor only; no training required.

ideas.question: How much head diversity can a low-rank residual recover over shared KV in a tiny synthetic attention task?

ideas.falsifier: If low-rank residuals offer no advantage over GQA/shared baselines, keep as source note.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Small linear algebra sweeps, likely C++/NumPy-friendly.

ideas.name: Native residual/KV sensitivity phase diagram
ideas.question: When does storing residual checkpoints beat full KV or lossy windows once recompute, bandwidth, and exactness are all explicit?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ cost sweep over context length, checkpoint period, exactness penalty, bandwidth weight, and compute weight.
ideas.falsifier: If residual checkpoints win all regimes under any constants, the probe is too biased and must be rebalanced.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Pure cost/proxy model; C++ makes large sweeps cheap.

ideas.name: Query movement phase-boundary scan
ideas.question: Where is the actual boundary between moving queries, moving cache blocks, local recompute, and index-then-fetch?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ sensitivity scan over fabric, shards, selected blocks, block size, and query payload.
ideas.falsifier: If one policy wins every scenario, constants are not informative enough.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Systems arithmetic is ideal for native microkernels.

ideas.name: LRKV head-diversity capacity probe
ideas.question: Can low-rank head residuals recover specialist-head information that shared KV or GQA erase?
ideas.minimum_test: Synthetic heads with shared and orthogonal roles; compare full MHA, shared KV, GQA, K=V proxy, and LRKV ranks.
ideas.falsifier: If LRKV never beats shared/GQA at equal score, demote from P0.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Small linear algebra and known synthetic factors; C++ is enough.

ideas.name: SANTA stochastic sparse-attention estimator wind tunnel
ideas.question: Does post-softmax value-row sampling fail on rare high-value tails, and can stratification or value-aware sampling repair it?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ compare top-k, post-softmax MC, stratified MC, and value-aware top-k across entropy/rare-tail regimes.

ideas.name: KV-CAT representation-compressibility proxy
ideas.question: Is compressibility a property of representation geometry as much as compressor choice?

ideas.question: Are we reinventing sparse-routing policies separately in every probe instead of using a small common policy vocabulary?

ideas.name: Graph-structured agent/session memory toy
ideas.question: When does graph session memory preserve decisions/rationale under a tighter budget than flat summary text?

ideas.name: Gist sparse-attention unfold trap
ideas.question: Can coarse gist summaries route to isolated rare raw chunks without retaining everything?
ideas.minimum_test: Chunk/gist/unfold toy with local summaries, recursive gist-of-gist, and rare isolated evidence.

ideas.name: Conversation-level agent-serving scheduler toy

ideas.minimum_test: Cost model over multi-turn traces with tool calls; compare per-turn prediction, conversation-level observation, and oracle scheduler.

ideas.name: Hybrid head-type compression toy
ideas.question: Do static and dynamic heads really need different cache compression policies in synthetic multimodal/text mixtures?

ideas.name: Native HPO phase-boundary harness
ideas.question: Can optimizer-state plus domain-prior proposals map CloudtainerML phase diagrams better than grids or random search?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ optimizer arena over synthetic cache/needle/deceptive landscapes with grid, random, prior-only, CEM, and Centaur-style state-prior hybrid.

ideas.name: Structure-aware on-demand hypergraph memory
ideas.question: Does query-triggered structure/hypergraph exploration beat flat top-k retrieval for scattered evidence under equal budget?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ long-document toy with sections, cross-section evidence, decoys, order constraints, and stale experience traces.
ideas.falsifier: If hierarchy/hypergraph routing loses to flat semantic top-k except in hand-tuned easy cases, demote.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Graph retrieval simulation is a native microkernel, no model training required.

ideas.name: Persistent memory sycophancy red-team

ideas.name: DF-SSM 1-bit scaffold plus low-rank correction toy

ideas.name: Long-output KV importance flow

ideas.name: Concrete episode memory beats abstract intent

ideas.name: GASLoC local-update communication toy
ideas.question: When do local optimizer steps plus sparse gossip beat synchronized averaging for tiny distributed training?

ideas.name: Future-failure prefix predictor
ideas.question: Can search traces reveal future failure early enough to steer before terminal reward?

ideas.falsifier: If future behavior is only predictable after the failure state is already visible, demote.

ideas.question: Is online prompt adaptation a useful memory object, and when does it become stale-state interference?
ideas.minimum_test: Prompt-state bandit with nonstationary tasks; compare persistent prompts, rollback checkpoints, per-task prompts, and no adaptation.
ideas.falsifier: If prompt state drifts catastrophically without simple task reset, treat as safety/monitoring lane.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Tiny symbolic/bandit simulation.

ideas.name: Quantization scale search for KV frontier
ideas.question: Does scale selection explain more output error than bit allocation in tiny KV quantization probes?
ideas.minimum_test: Add MSE/percentile/output-error scale selection to token-precision and KV wind-tunnel probes.
ideas.falsifier: If scale search does not move winner regions, keep focus on token selection and precision.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Native tensor probes can sweep scale cheaply.

ideas.name: Periodic reasoning-step cache rewrite
ideas.question: Are reasoning-step boundaries good times to rewrite/compress KV state compared with continuous eviction?
ideas.minimum_test: Multi-hop trace toy with step delimiters; compare continuous eviction, periodic consolidation, and oracle step rewrite.
ideas.falsifier: If step boundaries do not align with state changes, cache processors may need learned/event-driven boundaries.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Can be symbolic before training.

ideas.name: Verified lossy-cache guard
ideas.question: Can a cheap margin/drift/critical-step guard turn lossy KV compression into near-lossless behavior without full recompute?
ideas.minimum_test: Run experiments/vericache_guard/vericache_guard_probe.cpp and compare lossy, periodic, margin, drift, toy verifier, and oracle guards.
ideas.falsifier: If selective guards either miss catastrophic sites or recompute nearly everything, demote to systems-only curiosity.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Pure C++ decode-drift simulator with hundreds of seeds and no model weights.

ideas.name: Reasoning-step cache rewrite clock
ideas.question: Do explicit reasoning-step boundaries provide a better compression/rewrite clock than continuous eviction?
ideas.minimum_test: Run experiments/periodic_cache_rewrite/step_rewrite_probe.cpp across chain, early-premise, noisy-delimiter, recurrent-definition, and mostly-local regimes.
ideas.falsifier: If boundaries are not predictive or noisy delimiters erase the advantage, use event detectors rather than hard delimiters.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Symbolic trace simulator; no neural training needed.

ideas.name: Persistent-memory provenance phase diagram
ideas.question: When does persistent memory improve answers, and when does it amplify remembered user misconceptions?
ideas.minimum_test: Run experiments/memory_provenance_phase/memory_provenance_phase.cpp sweeping misbelief, correction loss, and high-stakes rate.
ideas.falsifier: If provenance/correction-linked policies do not beat no-memory in risky regimes, persistent memory should remain off by default there.
ideas.why_scale_fits: C++ phase sweep; useful even as a symbolic safety red-team.
ideas.charter_role: side-wing unless it directly improves tiny-scale performance/correctness metrics

ideas.name: Fixed-size tensor memory as object frontier
ideas.question: Should long-horizon state be stored as KV rows, residual checkpoints, fast-weight matrices, or a fixed tensor/grid state?
ideas.minimum_test: Moving-object/fact grid toy with occlusion and delayed queries; compare recency KV, Tensor Cache-like L2, and fixed tensor memory.
ideas.falsifier: If the spatial tensor only helps when the task leaks coordinates, keep it as a modality-specific branch.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Small 2D/3D arrays and C++ transition loops fit the cloudtainer.

ideas.name: CSR asynchronous reconciliation toy
ideas.question: Can asynchronous state reconciliation avoid latency spikes while preserving needed long-horizon state?
ideas.minimum_test: Agent trajectory simulator with prefix-stable state, pause windows, async eviction work, and spike-sensitive latency score.
ideas.falsifier: If async reconciliation merely hides work without preserving recall, demote to systems note.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Discrete-event C++ scheduler.

ideas.name: Learned history gate versus always-history
ideas.question: When is no memory better than always appending history, and can a gate learn that boundary?
ideas.minimum_test: Mixed Markovian/non-Markovian episode toy; compare no-history, always-history, heuristic-gated, and trained-gated recall.
ideas.falsifier: If a simple recency/history length rule matches learned gates, use that as baseline for memory policies.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Symbolic or tiny supervised classifier.

ideas.name: Reasoning Cache iterative improve/summarize loop
ideas.question: Can short-horizon update rules improve over longer test-time horizons by alternating response and summary state?
ideas.minimum_test: Toy proof/search environment with statement generation and lossy summary update; compare plain chain, periodic summary, and learned summary.
ideas.falsifier: If summary loops collapse into stale-state self-confirmation, keep stronger verifier/rewrite guards.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Tiny algorithmic environment, possibly C++ rollout plus Python training later.

ideas.name: Lossless acceptance tests for lossy probes
ideas.question: Should every lossy cache probe include an exact-output or catastrophic-divergence check, not only average reconstruction error?
ideas.minimum_test: Add catastrophic tail metrics to token-precision, SANTA, Express, and Tensor Cache probes.
ideas.falsifier: If tail metrics never disagree with mean error, keep dashboards simpler.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Audit/report layer only; cheap and high leverage.

ideas.name: Conversation-level scheduling as observable phase split
ideas.question: Is the right unit for agentic serving a whole conversation rather than individual turns?
ideas.minimum_test: Discrete-event toy with first-turn prefill, KV transfer, tail decode, tool pauses, and per-turn prediction error.
ideas.falsifier: If per-turn routing wins under low prediction error and low transfer cost, identify the phase boundary.
ideas.why_scale_fits: C++ event simulator with synthetic workloads.

ideas.name: Cache taxonomy audit row on every probe
ideas.question: Can we make every probe declare whether it is eviction, compression, hybrid memory, new attention, scheduling, safety, or representation training?
ideas.minimum_test: Add a taxonomy field to probe outputs and dashboard grouping.
ideas.falsifier: If taxonomy adds clerical burden without improving priority choices, keep it as docs only.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Refactor/audit task.

ideas.name: Safety-subspace cache quantization tails
ideas.question: Can a cache quantizer look good on mean reconstruction while flipping a low-dimensional alignment feature?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ alignment-subspace quant probe with safety projection flips and p99 safety error.
ideas.falsifier: If safety-tail ranking matches mean task MSE everywhere, demote to dashboard metric only.
ideas.why_scale_fits: C++ vector microkernel; no model required.
ideas.charter_role: side-wing unless it directly improves tiny-scale performance/correctness metrics

ideas.name: FlowTracer-style reasoning credit toy
ideas.question: Does answer-targeted flow through attention DAGs identify useful reasoning tokens better than local attention mass?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ reasoning DAG generator with bridge tokens, decoys, local formatting flood, and answer-region flow scoring.
ideas.falsifier: If local attention mass dominates flow in all regimes, keep only simple credit heuristics.
ideas.why_scale_fits: C++ graph traversal and scoring.

ideas.name: Partial-order mask frontier
ideas.question: Can mask design be scored as reachability plus leakage instead of a vague attention pattern?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ required/forbidden reachability toy across causal, block generation, prefix verification, and butterfly-style masks.
ideas.falsifier: If exact task masks always win trivially and no generalization question appears, keep as theory notes.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Small graph transitive-closure simulator.

ideas.name: Topic document vs temporal graph memory
ideas.question: When do topic documents beat flat records, and when does a temporal confidence graph need to preserve parallel revisions?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ streaming fact/revision simulator with flat recency, flat confidence, topic docs, temporal graph, non-destructive graph, and oracle latest-valid baselines.
ideas.falsifier: If flat recency wins under all change rates, demote graph memory.
ideas.why_scale_fits: C++ symbolic memory simulator.
ideas.charter_role: side-wing unless it directly improves tiny-scale performance/correctness metrics

ideas.name: Tail-risk contract for lossy probes
ideas.question: Which lossy/compressed probes still lack catastrophic-tail or exactness metrics?
ideas.minimum_test: Add tail_risk_report.py over current probe artifacts and flag missing tail contracts.
ideas.falsifier: If tail contracts add no new ranking information after a few hardening passes, simplify.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Python audit/report layer.

ideas.name: Probe taxonomy audit
ideas.question: Can the cube separate cache compression, safety tails, agent memory, reasoning credit, attention architecture, and meta-optimization in dashboards?
ideas.minimum_test: Add probe_taxonomy_audit.py and taxonomy fields to new probes.
ideas.falsifier: If taxonomy does not change priority calls, reduce to docs.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Python index/report layer.
ideas.charter_role: side-wing unless it directly improves tiny-scale performance/correctness metrics

ideas.name: False-success lightweight monitor
ideas.question: Can a cheap detector beat judge-like completion claims when environment state says failure?
ideas.minimum_test: Generate symbolic agent traces with explicit completion language and hidden state labels; compare surface judge, TF-IDF-ish detector, and state verifier.
ideas.falsifier: If environment-state verification is always trivial, construct partial-observability regimes.
ideas.why_scale_fits: C++/Python synthetic agent trajectories.

ideas.name: Multi-domain agent stress microbenchmark
ideas.question: What is the smallest multi-domain agent benchmark that stresses memory, task switching, verification, and tool-state correctness?
ideas.minimum_test: Interleave tiny customer-service domains and require correct state transitions across turns.
ideas.falsifier: If one-domain toy already captures failures, defer multi-domain expansion.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Symbolic environment; no LLM required.

ideas.name: Reasoning alignment regression toy
ideas.question: Can reasoning-oriented updates improve task score while damaging safety canaries or long-context recall?
ideas.minimum_test: Two-objective synthetic post-training loop with reasoning reward and safety/privacy canary projections.
ideas.falsifier: If tradeoffs are too dependent on hand-coded weights, wait for trained tiny model.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Small PyTorch or C++ optimizer toy.

ideas.name: Latent/discrete reasoning router revisit
ideas.question: When should a toy model spend visible tokens versus latent steps?
ideas.minimum_test: Use narrative/retrieval toy with explicit vs latent compute budget and utility penalties.
ideas.falsifier: If latent route is just a scalar compression trick, keep under latent-compute P1.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Could be Python training or C++ simulator.

ideas.name: Native HPO for safety-tail phase diagrams
ideas.question: Can the HPO phase harness find safety-tail phase transitions better than hand-picked probe constants?
ideas.minimum_test: Implemented in C++ as experiments/safety_tail_phase/safety_tail_phase.cpp; compare search policies for hidden tail phase discovery.

ideas.why_scale_fits: C++ microkernel + Python reporting.
ideas.charter_role: side-wing unless it directly improves tiny-scale performance/correctness metrics

ideas.name: Tail contract normal form patcher
ideas.question: Can every lossy/cache/memory-selection probe declare whether it has direct catastrophic-tail metrics, surrogate tail contracts, or still needs hardening?
ideas.minimum_test: Run tools/tail_contract_patcher.py over current-revision probe artifacts before tail_risk_report.py.
ideas.falsifier: If the patcher hides missing science behind schema, keep it as audit-only and require direct tail metrics for promotion.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Pure Python artifact audit/refactor.

ideas.name: Goal-conditioned distortion fact-pool probe
ideas.question: Can a system produce misleading outputs using only true facts, by selecting/softening/omitting adverse facts under a goal?
ideas.minimum_test: Implemented in C++ as JANUS-style fixed fact-pool selection with adverse/favorable coverage and distortion metrics.
ideas.falsifier: If balanced provenance contracts and goal-biased methods score similarly across regimes, deprioritize.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Symbolic C++ simulator; no model weights needed.
ideas.charter_role: side-wing unless it directly improves tiny-scale performance/correctness metrics

ideas.name: Provenance gate plus adaptive recovery
ideas.question: Do provenance-grounded gates catch failures missed by reward gates, and can rejected samples be repaired without naive resampling?
ideas.minimum_test: Implemented in C++ with reward-only, provenance-only, dual, adaptive recovery, and naive resample policies.
ideas.falsifier: If recovery only increases yield by accepting invalid samples, keep as safety negative.
ideas.why_scale_fits: C++ event simulator; can later become a data-curation harness.
ideas.charter_role: side-wing unless it directly improves tiny-scale performance/correctness metrics

ideas.name: Predictor-gated bank-wise sparse channel routing
ideas.question: Does bank-wise top-k routing avoid rare bank starvation and layer-local long-context failures better than global top-k?
ideas.minimum_test: Implemented C++ channel routing simulator with bank-wise, global, random, oracle, and single-layer repair.
ideas.falsifier: If global top-k always dominates under equal FLOPs, bank-wise diversity is less interesting at toy scale.
ideas.why_scale_fits: C++ microkernel over synthetic channel importance distributions.

ideas.name: Predictive prefill chunk anchors
ideas.question: Do periodic chunk anchors reduce lost-in-the-middle failures under sparse chunk retrieval?
ideas.minimum_test: Implemented C++ chunk selection simulator with top-k chunks, anchors, dense baseline, and oracle chunks.
ideas.falsifier: If anchors only help because they leak target positions, redesign with harder distractor-anchor regimes.
ideas.why_scale_fits: C++ simulator; directly maps to chunk routing/cost phase diagrams.

ideas.name: Recall-preserving rerank cascade
ideas.question: When is it better to protect recall first and spend compute only on reranking a small fixed candidate set?
ideas.minimum_test: Future cascade toy: top-10 candidate recall fixed; compare rerank quality and anti-shortcut ablations.
ideas.falsifier: If candidate set quality is too hand-coded, wait for real retrieval traces.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Small Python/C++ ranking simulator.

ideas.name: Linear-constrained vector quantization toy
ideas.question: Can a linear-constrained codebook give a better 2-bit reconstruction/optimization frontier than scalar quantization on tiny matrices?
ideas.minimum_test: Tiny differentiable VQ codebook simulator, maybe Python first.
ideas.falsifier: If the benefit disappears under equal overhead and no learned codebooks, keep as paper note.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Small matrices and synthetic gradients.

ideas.name: Curriculum graph knowledge-gap signal
ideas.question: Can graph-aware topic signals find root causes of repeated failures better than raw frequency counts?
ideas.minimum_test: Synthetic prerequisite DAG and question stream with hidden gap topics.
ideas.falsifier: If raw frequency and graph centrality are indistinguishable, keep outside P0.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Tiny graph simulation.

ideas.name: Trustworthy memory search filter
ideas.question: Should memory search return objective evidence, user beliefs, corrections, and preferences as separate typed objects rather than one ranked list?
ideas.minimum_test: Extend memory provenance/sycophancy probes with search-stage trust filters and object types.
ideas.falsifier: If typing does not reduce sycophancy/leakage in adversarial regimes, focus on write-time filters.
ideas.why_scale_fits: C++ symbolic memory search; no LLM needed.

ideas.name: Memory Poisoning Trust-Gate Wind Tunnel
ideas.question: When does a single adversarial write survive memory admission and later dominate retrieval despite low average utility impact?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Candidate memory ranking and poisoning propagation are small symbolic/vector simulations well suited to C++.
ideas.minimum_test: Generate benign/poison candidate memory sets and compare similarity-only, write-time filters, read-time gates, query-conditioned gates, provenance decay, and oracle trust boundaries.
ideas.falsifier: If similarity-only is never vulnerable once utility is controlled, the toy is too weak or poisoning is not the first P0 target.
ideas.charter_role: side-wing unless it directly improves tiny-scale performance/correctness metrics

ideas.name: Execution-State Tree Memory
ideas.question: Does path/tree memory preserve long-horizon state integrity better than semantic retrieval when traces branch or contain errors?
ideas.why_scale_fits: State trees, branch errors, and trace contamination can be tested with cheap synthetic C++ trajectories.
ideas.minimum_test: Compare full context, semantic retrieval, flat summaries, active path tree, maintain/revise, sibling hints, and oracle active path.
ideas.falsifier: If active path memory does not beat semantic retrieval under branching/error regimes, demote Mage-like tree memory until the task is made more realistic.
ideas.charter_role: side-wing unless it directly improves tiny-scale performance/correctness metrics

ideas.name: Equal-Cost Sparse Prefill Chunk Anchors
ideas.question: Do chunk anchors still help when dense baselines are forced onto the same token/compute budget?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Chunk-routing, boundary needles, lost-middle, and distractor anchors are tiny deterministic simulations.
ideas.minimum_test: Rebuild the previous sparse prefill toy under equal token budgets instead of letting dense read everything cheaply.
ideas.falsifier: If anchors lose at equal cost except oracle cases, keep them P1 and focus on forecast/query routers instead.

ideas.name: Agent Memory Lifecycle Cost Frontier
ideas.question: At what query volume and freshness/mutation rate does expensive structured memory construction pay back?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Lifecycle cost is a phase diagram; C++ can sweep many query-volume and mutation regimes quickly.
ideas.minimum_test: Compare BM25, embedding RAG, structured triples, agentic control flow, on-demand structure, freshness-scheduled hybrid, and oracle.
ideas.falsifier: If construction cost never changes the winner, the cost model is too flat and should be replaced by measured timings later.

ideas.name: Active Graph Reconstruction, Not Static Retrieval
ideas.question: Can bounded iterative graph reconstruction recover multi-hop evidence with less token cost than static top-k retrieval?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Cue-tag-content graphs and bounded expansion are easy synthetic graph tasks.
ideas.minimum_test: Build query-specific graph walks that alternate expansion and pruning and compare to static retrieval/reranking.
ideas.falsifier: If active reconstruction only helps with oracle edges, keep graph memory below tree/execution-state memory.

ideas.name: Head-Aware KV Cache Object
ideas.question: When does per-head cache management beat monolithic token-level cache management on tail accuracy and cost?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Head-role heterogeneity can be simulated with local/global/random heads before touching real models.
ideas.minimum_test: Create synthetic heads with different distance/range/value functions and sweep monolithic vs head-aware budgets.
ideas.falsifier: If head-aware allocation only helps when the head taxonomy is leaked, demote to systems note.

ideas.name: Curvature-Conditioned Linear Attention Readout
ideas.question: Can query-side conditioning reduce target dilution in linear/associative memory without adding full attention?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Associative recall already exists; this is a readout modification and phase diagram.
ideas.minimum_test: Extend spectral associative recall with query curvature signals and compare against additive memory, delta memory, and attention oracle.
ideas.falsifier: If target dilution remains unchanged, move back to write-side memory gates.

ideas.name: Query-Participating State Evolution
ideas.question: Does allowing queries to influence memory state updates help corrections, overwrites, or delayed recall?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Small recurrent-state simulations can isolate write/read mechanisms cheaply.
ideas.minimum_test: Compare key-only updates, delta updates, gated erase/write, and query-conditioned updates on correction/reversal tasks.
ideas.falsifier: If query participation only memorizes recent queries and hurts stable facts, keep it out of the P0 set.

ideas.name: Low-Rank Decay Grokking Clock
ideas.question: Does low-rank decay make a tiny model simplify after interpolation when L2 no longer changes the spectrum?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Modular arithmetic grokking is data-small and CPU-feasible if we keep models tiny.
ideas.minimum_test: Train tiny MLP/attention models on modular arithmetic under no decay, L2 decay, and low-rank decay; log singular spectrum and generalization clock.
ideas.falsifier: If the run cost is too high or no delayed generalization appears, leave as deferred tiny-training lane.

ideas.name: Causal Stack-State Interventions
ideas.question: Can we force stack-like internal state edits in tiny formal-language models and change outputs predictably?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Counter languages and stack automata are tiny, inspectable, and CPU-trainable.
ideas.minimum_test: Train a tiny model on counter/parentheses language, infer stack-state direction, intervene, and compare causal output changes.
ideas.falsifier: If interventions do not change behavior beyond noise, keep only representation diagnostics.

ideas.name: Trajectory Geometry Monitor
ideas.question: Can probe-free representation-trajectory metrics reveal phase transitions before task metrics move?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Works as an analysis tool on any tiny trained model once we have hidden-state dumps.
ideas.minimum_test: Add trajectory metrics to DFS/SMT/grokking runs and compare to loss/accuracy change points.
ideas.falsifier: If geometry metrics are noisy and non-predictive at tiny scale, drop to appendix.

ideas.name: Agent State Variability Battery
ideas.question: How much of agent-output variability comes from memory state/update policy rather than stochastic sampling alone?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Stateful tree/search agents can be simulated without large models.
ideas.minimum_test: Run deterministic policy with varied memory write/retrieve/update seeds and quantify divergence, false success, and replay stability.
ideas.falsifier: If variability is dominated by trivial random seeds, merge this with DFS/TRACE instead of a standalone lane.

ideas.name: Memory Admissibility HPO Gate
ideas.question: Can a cheap admissibility contract, tuned over trust/provenance thresholds, reduce memory poisoning without deleting useful memories?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Pure synthetic candidate-memory scoring is perfect for C++ phase sweeps.
ideas.minimum_test: Run memory_admissibility_hpo.cpp over sleeper, cross-domain, stale-correction, and benign regimes.
ideas.falsifier: If gates only reduce attacks by rejecting nearly all valid memory, keep as safety warning but drop from main build.
ideas.charter_role: side-wing unless it directly improves tiny-scale performance/correctness metrics

ideas.name: Execution-State Verification and Revise Boundaries
ideas.question: Do Maintain/Revise-style execution-state operations beat semantic retrieval and full traces when errors branch and false success appears?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Synthetic branch traces and false-success traps are cheap and observable.
ideas.minimum_test: Run execution_state_verify_probe.cpp and inspect state integrity, contamination, recovery, and utility.
ideas.falsifier: If verification boundaries are not better than active-path or full-trace baselines, search for sharper error regimes before training.
ideas.charter_role: side-wing unless it directly improves tiny-scale performance/correctness metrics

ideas.name: Evidence Provenance DAG
ideas.question: Should memory items be scored as evidence DAG nodes with source/revision/contradiction metadata rather than text chunks?
ideas.why_scale_fits: All variables are discrete or scalar; no model training needed to test the scoring failure modes.
ideas.minimum_test: Run evidence_provenance_dag_probe.cpp with stale updates, contaminated tools, and conflict resolution regimes.
ideas.falsifier: If provenance-aware scoring does not beat relevance/source-only except oracle cases, it may be audit vocabulary rather than active algorithm.
ideas.charter_role: side-wing unless it directly improves tiny-scale performance/correctness metrics

ideas.name: Dual-Horizon Memory Retrieval
ideas.question: When do global episode memories and local turn memories need separate retrieval policies?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Interactive task stages can be simulated with scalar global/local utility and stage-shift variables.
ideas.minimum_test: Run horizon_memory_retrieval_probe.cpp; compare episode-only, turn-only, dual-static, and PRM-like policies.
ideas.falsifier: If dual horizon never beats single-horizon baselines at equal budget, park until trained agents exist.

ideas.name: Support-Path Persona Memory
ideas.question: Can evidence→pattern→claim support paths prevent overconfident unsupported user/person claims?
ideas.why_scale_fits: A small tree of evidence and abstractions can be simulated without personal data or real deployment.
ideas.minimum_test: Build a support-path toy with claims, evidence count, conflicts, confidence, and query-conditioned retrieval depth.
ideas.falsifier: If support paths just act like source-weighted retrieval, merge into provenance DAG.

ideas.name: Residual Experience Delta Trees
ideas.question: Can near-repeat experiences be stored as deltas rather than full traces without losing rare environment differences?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Delta-tree costs and errors are cheap to simulate in C++.
ideas.minimum_test: Compare append-only, merge-summary, and delta-tree memories over near-repeat tasks with rare divergences.
ideas.falsifier: If deltas erase rare differences under modest noise, keep as a red-team regime for experience memory.

ideas.name: Triggered Multimodal Memory Poisoning Trap
ideas.question: Can dormant trigger-conditioned memory poisoning evade same-session memory audits?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Trigger variables and delayed activation can be modeled symbolically before any image/audio work.
ideas.minimum_test: Extend memory admissibility HPO with dormant triggers and measure activation after benign retrieval.
ideas.falsifier: If trigger conditioning is equivalent to existing delayed-activation regimes, do not create a separate lane.

ideas.name: Text World Model State Transition Toy
ideas.question: Can a tiny learned or symbolic text-world transition model detect memory/state impossibilities better than retrieval?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Toy textual state machines are small enough for Python/C++ and later tiny models.
ideas.minimum_test: Build state/action/observation triples and compare reactive, retrieved, and transition-predicted state validators.
ideas.falsifier: If transition prediction is only memorization, postpone until trained DFS/SMT environments.

ideas.name: Memory Anomaly Ops Taxonomy Audit
ideas.question: Can every memory/cache failure in the cube be typed as a short-context, long-memory, evidence, execution-state, or governance anomaly?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Pure audit/refactor pass over existing probe metadata.
ideas.minimum_test: Add taxonomy fields to probe outputs and a report that groups failures by anomaly class.
ideas.falsifier: If the taxonomy is too vague to change priorities, keep it as docs only.

ideas.name: Perturbation-Aware Multimodal Budget Toy
ideas.question: Do modality-specific perturbation sensitivities beat generic attention/mass scoring under a fixed memory budget?
ideas.why_scale_fits: A toy two-modality signal with different perturbation curves is easy to sweep.
ideas.minimum_test: Simulate audio-like and visual-like channels with different sensitivity and query mixtures.
ideas.falsifier: If generic salience wins under all mixes, keep multimodal budget as deferred.

ideas.name: Project Charter Focus Guard
ideas.question: Can the cube keep security/trust/state-boundary material as a small side wing while the core remains tiny-scale performance, architecture, and surprise discovery?
ideas.why_scale_fits: Pure audit/refactor work over docs and ledgers; it protects project direction without adding training burden.
ideas.minimum_test: Add a charter file, priority reset, and current-surface audit that checks whether root docs promote performance/architecture first and security only as a bounded wing.
ideas.falsifier: If the audit becomes vague or prevents interesting performance probes from being added, delete or weaken it.

ideas.name: Component-Aware Low-Rank Rank Allocation
ideas.question: Can QK, OV, and MLP rank budgets be allocated by functional fragility rather than uniform rank or raw spectral energy?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ component_rank_allocator probe with equal total rank budgets and synthetic component spectra/sensitivities.
ideas.falsifier: If uniform/parameter-weighted allocation always matches component-functional allocation across fragility regimes, deprioritize A3-style tiny rank sweeps.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Only spectra, rank allocation, and scalar functional losses are needed before touching a trained model.

ideas.name: Gated Subspace Inference Residual Impact Gate
ideas.question: When can a cheap per-token gate skip residual corrections without losing exactness or creating rare high-impact misses?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ gated_subspace_inference probe comparing full linear, subspace-only, norm gates, predictive gates, and oracle gates.
ideas.falsifier: If cheap gates cannot beat full computation under any cost/error regime, keep as a cautionary negative until a trained gate exists.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Activation-manifold and residual-impact distributions can be synthesized and swept in C++.

ideas.name: Exact/Linear Attention Discriminability Wind Tunnel
ideas.question: Do positive/linear kernels fail by target-mass dilution even when they look cheap and stable?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ ELA dilution probe over context length, decoy rate, temperature, and kernel family.
ideas.falsifier: If linear kernels preserve target mass and output under all long/distractor regimes, escalate to tiny trained linear-attention blocks.
ideas.why_scale_fits: No training required: attention mass and value-output error are enough for a first falsifier.

ideas.name: Low-Rank Decay Spectral Grokking Dynamics
ideas.question: Does LRD-style spectral shrinkage have a tiny visible advantage over L2 decay after memorization gradients vanish?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ singular-spectrum dynamics with signal/noise ranks, data fraction, and overregularization traps.
ideas.falsifier: If LRD and L2 produce indistinguishable effective-rank/generalization proxies under scale-invariant post-memorization dynamics, delay trained grokking runs.
ideas.why_scale_fits: The core claim is spectral and can be probed before expensive modular-arithmetic training.

ideas.name: Attention Dilution Eviction as a Performance Win

ideas.name: Operator/Router Family Report Refactor
ideas.question: Can the cube compare operator/router/ranker/MoE probes without mixing them into a generic native leaderboard?
ideas.minimum_test: tools/operator_route_report.py scans current artifacts for cost fields, failure fields, fresh/carry-forward status, and winner diversity.
ideas.falsifier: If the report duplicates existing dashboards without steering priorities, remove from smoke-required artifacts.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Report-only refactor.

ideas.name: Spectral Operator HPO Sweep
ideas.question: Can DCT/spectral operator routing beat fixed DCT+attention residuals on held-out regimes once alias/tail/cost fields are scored?
ideas.minimum_test: experiments/spectral_operator_hpo_sweep/spectral_operator_hpo_sweep.cpp performs held-out threshold/residual-budget HPO over actual DCT/IDCT transforms.
ideas.falsifier: If selected HPO config loses to fixed DCT+attention on held-out regimes or hides alias/tail misses, keep CHIAR-style routing as P1 only.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Pure C++ DCT/IDCT synthetic signals; hundreds to thousands of rows in milliseconds/seconds.

ideas.name: Copy-Head Phase Transition Screen
ideas.question: Can tiny copy-task phase probes distinguish abrupt softmax emergence from smoother linear/annealed emergence before training a transformer?
ideas.minimum_test: experiments/copy_head_phase_transition/copy_head_phase_probe.cpp sweeps sample count, sequence length, vocab size, and attention family; records loss, precursor, abruptness, and monitor risk.
ideas.falsifier: If the screen merely rewards low compute and never exposes sharp copy emergence, escalate to a real tiny trained copy-head model or demote.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Analytical/symbolic phase probe is tiny and directly maps to training-data/sequence-size sweeps.

ideas.name: Expert-Choice Sparse Attention Frontier
ideas.question: When does MoSA-style head-specific content sparsity beat LoLA-style sparse caching, local windows, and dense attention under equal-cost scoring?
ideas.minimum_test: experiments/expert_choice_sparse_attention/expert_choice_sparse_attention.cpp compares dense, uniform sparse, cluster routing, expert-choice sparse attention, LoLA cache, and hybrid policies.
ideas.falsifier: If dense or a trivial local/cache baseline dominates all regimes once tail miss and head collision are scored, do not train this lane yet.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Symbolic C++ routing/retrieval regimes; no GPU required.

ideas.name: Gated Bidirectional Linear Attention Frontier
ideas.question: Are local mixing, key gating/forgetting, and output gating enough to make bidirectional linear attention competitive on long-history retrieval toys?
ideas.minimum_test: experiments/gated_bidirectional_linear/gated_bidirectional_linear.cpp scores quality, cost, forgetting, local miss, and latency proxy across history lengths.
ideas.falsifier: If GBLA-style all-in only wins due to over-friendly symbolic constants, require actual matrix/kernel probe before promotion.
ideas.why_scale_fits: C++ symbolic frontier over long histories and budgets.

ideas.name: Confidence-Adaptive SwiGLU MoE Guard
ideas.question: Does confidence-adaptive activation compute help, or does it fail exactly where router confidence is wrong or rare experts matter?
ideas.minimum_test: experiments/confidence_adaptive_swiglu/confidence_adaptive_swiglu.cpp compares dense, standard top-k, confidence-adaptive, rare-guard, tiny-linear, and fallback policies.
ideas.falsifier: If confidence-only wins by ignoring rare misses and route flips, require rare-expert guard fields before promotion.
ideas.why_scale_fits: MoE activation costs/quality symbolic wind tunnel runs cheaply in C++.

ideas.name: Spectral Operator Report Refactor
ideas.question: Can the cube compare spectral/operator probes separately from generic router and native dashboards?
ideas.minimum_test: tools/spectral_operator_report.py scans current spectral artifacts for freshness, HPO pressure, winner diversity, alias/tail/regret guards, and readiness.
ideas.falsifier: If the report duplicates operator_route_report without steering the next trained escalation, delete it.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Report-only refactor.

ideas.name: Novelty / Salience Audit Discipline
ideas.question: Which CloudtainerML observations look genuinely surprising or under-mentioned, and which are only paper claims or toy artifacts?
ideas.minimum_test: Create NOVELTY-HYPOTHESES.md, PROJECT-SALIENCE.md, and tools/novelty_salience_audit.py; rank surprise claims by evidence strength and novelty caution.
ideas.falsifier: If the audit cannot separate internal evidence from external paper claims and speculation, it should not steer priorities.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Report-only audit over existing probe outputs and ledgers; no new training required.

ideas.name: Tiny Copy-Head Trained Escalation
ideas.question: Does a minimal trained pointer-copy model show different emergence smoothness and speed across softmax, sparsemax, relu-normalized, and cosine/no-exp attention?
ideas.minimum_test: experiments/tiny_copy_head_training/tiny_copy_head_train.py trains four one-query pointer-copy variants and writes REV0032_TINY_COPY_HEAD_TRAINING_SMOKE.json/csv.
ideas.falsifier: If all variants learn with identical curves and no target-mass/transition-width distinction, the symbolic copy-phase lane should be demoted until a better task is built.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Tiny PyTorch training completes in seconds on CPU; the task is deliberately small enough to be rerun often.

ideas.name: xLSTM State-Correction Wind Tunnel
ideas.question: Is robust state correction the mechanism that makes gated subquadratic architectures attractive at tiny scale?
ideas.minimum_test: experiments/xlstm_state_correction/xlstm_state_correction.cpp compares additive, fixed decay, residual gate, xLSTM-like input/forget gate, and oracle correction.
ideas.falsifier: If fixed decay dominates once noise, resets, and correction lags are scored fairly, the xLSTM correction intuition is not useful for our tiny probes.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Scalar/vector state tracking runs cheaply in C++ and produces broad phase rows.

ideas.name: No-Exp Oscillator Attention Proxy
ideas.question: When exponentials/global reductions are charged, can no-exp cosine/synchronization-style attention be competitive without losing tails?
ideas.minimum_test: experiments/oscillator_attention_proxy/oscillator_attention_proxy.cpp compares softmax, relu, cosine, oscillator-power proxy, and top-k softmax.
ideas.falsifier: If no-exp variants only win by dropping sharp/tail evidence, keep this as a hardware-regime curiosity rather than an architecture candidate.
ideas.why_scale_fits: C++ vector score simulator; cheap cost/quality phase screen.

ideas.name: Frequent Directions Streaming Memory Sketch
ideas.question: Can FD-style sketches preserve the right low-rank memory directions under drift without erasing rare directions?
ideas.minimum_test: Future C++ sketch frontier: exact covariance vs FD vs reservoir vs random projection on retrieval/streaming state tasks.
ideas.falsifier: If FD wins mean reconstruction but fails rare-direction veto tests, it stays a compression baseline only.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Streaming sketches are ideal C++ microkernel material.

ideas.name: Chain-of-Operators Harness Toy
ideas.question: Can explicit operator chains beat learned operator routing when the base model is frozen or tiny?
ideas.minimum_test: Future toy: simple function-family transforms with direct predictor vs pre/post explicit transform chains.
ideas.falsifier: If explicit chains only help where the answer transform is leaked, drop it.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Symbolic function operators are cheap; useful mainly as an analogy for operator routing.

ideas.name: Trained Escalation Report Refactor
ideas.question: Can the cube clearly separate trained tiny evidence from symbolic/native wind tunnel evidence?
ideas.minimum_test: tools/trained_escalation_report.py scans current trained artifacts for primary metrics, guard fields, and winner claims.
ideas.falsifier: If report duplicates generic dashboards without changing priority decisions, remove it.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Report-only audit; no extra compute.

ideas.name: Routing Absorption Gate Wind Tunnel
ideas.question: When do learned sparse-attention gates actually beat frozen random gates once representation co-adaptation is allowed?
ideas.minimum_test: Run experiments/routing_absorption_gate/routing_absorption_gate.cpp and inspect absorption_gap, deployment_loss, rare_miss, and score.
ideas.falsifier: If learned end-to-end gates beat random and posthoc gates across co-adapted, shifted, and rare-route regimes with low deployment loss, the absorption warning weakens.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Pure native C++ symbolic phase screen; no model training needed.

ideas.name: Directional Suppression Router Wind Tunnel
ideas.question: Is lightweight shared suppression routing useful because it coordinates heads, not because it increases individual head capacity?
ideas.minimum_test: Run experiments/directional_suppression_router/directional_suppression_router.cpp across domain-adaptive, syntactic, redundant, rare-direction, and noisy-induction regimes.
ideas.falsifier: If independent heads or vanilla attention dominate once ablation fragility and rare directions are scored, directional coordination is not a promotion candidate.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Synthetic C++ vector/score model; good before trained-router escalation.

ideas.name: Self-Routing Hidden-State Entropy Probe
ideas.question: Can hidden-state subspaces replace dedicated MoE routers at tiny scale, or does this only work when representations are already aligned?
ideas.minimum_test: Run experiments/self_routing_entropy/self_routing_entropy.cpp and compare learned, self, random, hash, dense, and oracle routing.
ideas.falsifier: If self-routing loses in hidden-aligned and balance-sensitive regimes, parameter-free routing should not be promoted.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Native C++ screening; later can become tiny MoE toy.

ideas.name: Contribution-Weight Geometry Guard
ideas.question: Should cache/attention retention be promoted only when it scores value magnitude and directional alignment, not attention mass alone?
ideas.minimum_test: Run experiments/contribution_weight_geometry/contribution_weight_geometry.cpp and inspect output_error, cancel_error, and tail_miss.
ideas.falsifier: If attention_mass_topk dominates in high-value/low-attention and cancellation regimes, contribution geometry is unnecessary.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Pure C++ guard field for many existing probes.

ideas.name: Routing Signature Telemetry Guard
ideas.question: Can a tiny router be audited through task-conditioned activation signatures before we trust downstream loss?
ideas.minimum_test: Attach route-signature entropy/clustering fields to MoE/router probes.
ideas.falsifier: If routing signatures do not separate synthetic task families better than random/load-balanced baselines, deprioritize telemetry.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Audit/reporting layer; no heavy training.

ideas.name: Adaptive Multi-Scale Expert Routing Toy
ideas.question: Does dynamic expert fusion over resampled temporal views reveal any tiny-scale performance win outside language-like tokens?
ideas.minimum_test: Build a C++ signal classifier toy with short/long/noisy periodic regimes and MoE multi-scale views.
ideas.falsifier: If fixed fusion beats dynamic routing under equal cost, park the lane.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Synthetic I/Q-like signals are cheap to generate.

ideas.name: Routing Family Absorption-vs-Coordination Split
ideas.question: Are routers useful only when they coordinate existing modules, and weak when they merely choose sparse entries that representations can absorb?
ideas.minimum_test: Compare routing_absorption_gate, directional_suppression_router, self_routing_entropy, DOT/MPI/ProbMoE, and spectral operator routing in one routing-family report.
ideas.falsifier: If gate-like token selection and coordination routers have indistinguishable failure modes, the split is probably overfit.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Report/refactor plus existing native probes.

ideas.name: Routing Family Report Refactor
ideas.question: Can the cube separate route-selection, route-coordination, route-telemetry, and route-absorption instead of putting every router in one bucket?
ideas.minimum_test: Run tools/routing_family_report.py and check current routing probes for absorption/cost/rare/coordination guard fields.
ideas.falsifier: If the report does not change prioritization or expose missing guard fields, remove it.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Static/report-only.

ideas.name: Tiny Routing Absorption Trained Escalation
ideas.question: When a sparse gate is trained jointly with attention, does soft training accuracy survive hard top-k deployment, or is posthoc gating over frozen dense geometry more reliable?
ideas.minimum_test: Run experiments/tiny_routing_absorption_train/tiny_routing_absorption_train.py on lookup/copy regimes and compare dense, oracle sparse, random sparse, soft end-to-end gate, hard deployed gate, and posthoc hard gate.
ideas.falsifier: If soft-gate and hard-gate deployment are always equivalent and posthoc gating never helps, routing absorption is less actionable at tiny scale.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Small synthetic lookup/copy task trains in seconds on CPU.

ideas.name: Boundary Reachability / Phase Guard
ideas.question: Can local sparse masks fail exact-copy tasks because the source is graph-unreachable despite being nearby?
ideas.minimum_test: Run boundary_reachability_repair.cpp and score fixed block, sliding-window, centered bridge, post-boundary bridge, source-extended bridge, periodic full, and dense oracle masks by reachability, boundary cliffs, and cost.
ideas.falsifier: If fixed blocks and repaired masks have identical reachability surfaces across phase/distance/depth, the boundary guard is not useful.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Pure graph coverage computation in C++ is extremely cheap and exact.

ideas.name: Exactness Guard Report Refactor
ideas.question: Which performance probes expose exact-copy, needle, reachability, route-flip, target-miss, or rare-token fields before they are promoted?
ideas.minimum_test: Run tools/exactness_guard_report.py and use it as a promotion surface for sparse/cache/routing/operator probes.
ideas.falsifier: If guard fields do not change any priority decisions, demote the report.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Report-only audit over existing JSON artifacts.

ideas.name: Sessa Feedback State Tail Probe
ideas.question: Does putting attention inside a recurrent feedback path create a different old-evidence decay law than one-shot attention plus recurrent state?
ideas.minimum_test: Build a C++ influence-tail simulator comparing transformer one-shot reads, Mamba-like fixed state, xLSTM-like gated correction, and Sessa-style feedback attention.
ideas.falsifier: If feedback attention does not change tail/retrieval surfaces under equal state cost, keep it P1 or retire.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Influence-tail equations and synthetic retrieval are cheap; no full LM needed.

ideas.name: Sparse Attention Program Schema
ideas.question: Can sparse attention mechanisms be represented as small source/write-back/reuse programs so C++ wind tunnels become comparable rather than bespoke?
ideas.minimum_test: Draft a schema that expresses block, bridge, sliding, top-k, shared-routing, ART termination, and MoSA/LoLA-like sparse-cache actions.
ideas.falsifier: If every mechanism needs special-case fields and no common guard metrics, the schema is too early.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Starts as an audit/refactor layer over current C++ probes.

ideas.name: Tiny Boundary Reachability Training
ideas.question: Does the boundary reachability cliff survive when a tiny attention model actually learns a copy task instead of only being scored by graph reachability?
ideas.minimum_test: Train one-head copy readers under fixed-block, sliding, source-bridge, post-boundary bridge, periodic skip, and full-causal masks.
ideas.falsifier: If fixed-block masks learn boundary copy without source reachability or if bridge/sliding masks do not separate cleanly, the symbolic reachability story is incomplete.
ideas.why_scale_fits: CPU PyTorch one-head task runs in seconds and directly tests exact-copy/reachability.

ideas.name: Sparse Attention Program Schema Wind Tunnel
ideas.question: Can block, sliding, bridge, periodic, and anchor sparse masks be compared as small reachability/cost programs with common guard fields?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ enumerator over mechanisms, lengths, block sizes, windows, periods, and target/source regimes.
ideas.falsifier: If common fields cannot explain winners or miss cases, return to bespoke probe families.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Pure graph/cost enumeration is fast and highly inspectable in C++.

ideas.name: Preconditioned Attention Conditioning Probe
ideas.question: Can attention preconditioning improve ill-conditioned attention geometry without erasing rare-axis signals?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ proxy comparing raw dot, whitening, ridge, clipped preconditioning, and over-whitening under anisotropic and rare-axis regimes.
ideas.falsifier: If conditioning only improves a proxy while increasing tail-risk/rare-axis failure, keep it as an optimizer note rather than architecture priority.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Condition-number and entropy proxies do not require training a full model.

ideas.name: Periodic Skip Off-Phase Trap
ideas.question: Do deterministic periodic skip edges create predictable long-range coverage but fail sharply on off-phase dependencies?
ideas.minimum_test: Represent periodic skip attention in the sparse program schema and compare off-phase target/source reachability to sliding/bridge/dense masks.
ideas.falsifier: If periodic skip never wins or fails everything under equal cost, demote until trained evidence appears.
ideas.why_scale_fits: A graph reachability/cost screen is enough for first falsification.

ideas.name: Entropy-Guided Progressive Depth Looping
ideas.question: Can high-entropy-head looping make tiny copy/head emergence smoother or faster than fixed recurrent depth?
ideas.minimum_test: Future trained-tiny copy or modular arithmetic task with fixed loop, entropy-triggered loop, and deep-to-shallow schedules.
ideas.falsifier: If entropy selects noisy heads or increases compute without faster convergence, keep this as a scaling-only curiosity.
ideas.why_scale_fits: A two-layer tiny attention model can expose head entropy and copy/order precursors.

ideas.name: Multi-Hop Boundary Reachability Training
ideas.question: Can depth repair a boundary miss only when the mask has an actual relay path, and can a tiny model learn that relay?
ideas.minimum_test: Train a multi-layer one-head reader on previous-block-source copy with fixed block, sliding, periodic, ring/anchor and boundary-bridge masks.
ideas.falsifier: If masks with no transitive source reachability learn the copy task anyway, the task has leakage or a shortcut and the earlier boundary claim weakens.
ideas.why_scale_fits: A CPU PyTorch model with 1–3 layers and 20-token sequences tests the mechanism directly.

ideas.name: Routing-Gain Decoupling Wind Tunnel
ideas.question: Can correct attention routing still fail because the selected value signal is too weak, and do gain-aware methods fix a different failure than sparse routing?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ proxy with route_error, gain_error, importance_error and target_miss across weak-evidence, distractor, and deep-attenuation regimes.
ideas.falsifier: If route-only attention and route+gain methods are indistinguishable once exactness/cost is charged, demote gain decoupling.
ideas.why_scale_fits: The first mechanism check is algebraic and does not need a trained LLM.

ideas.name: Sparse Program Page-Cost Reality Guard
ideas.question: Which sparse attention programs still win after selector overhead, page alignment, fusion, and exactness costs are charged?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ page-cost proxy comparing dense, static block, dynamic top-k, page-aligned block, fused vFlow-like and boundary-bridge sparse programs.
ideas.falsifier: If nominal sparse density predicts winners but wall_proxy and exact_miss reverse them, promotion must require page-cost fields.
ideas.why_scale_fits: A systems-shaped C++ proxy is enough to catch false speedups before kernel work.

ideas.name: Depth-Route Interpretability Guard
ideas.question: When do explicit depth-routing weights carry mechanism information rather than merely exposing a content-independent schedule?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ probe scoring content sensitivity, causal ablation match and confound penalty for posthoc schedules, learned routes and patch probes.
ideas.falsifier: If posthoc schedules pass causal/content tests, then the guard is too weak; if learned routes fail them, explicit routing alone should not be promoted.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Causal-probe proxies are cheap and clarify what a trained follow-up must measure.

ideas.name: Memory-Traffic First Attention Audit
ideas.question: Can we stop promoting efficient-attention ideas that reduce FLOPs but materialize expensive intermediates or ignore memory-bound execution?
ideas.minimum_test: Add a mechanism promotion report that flags memory traffic, intermediate materialization, selector cost and exactness-guard presence.
ideas.falsifier: If the audit does not change promotion decisions, fold it into screen-regret reporting instead.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Audit tooling is cheap and protects the project from misleading phase screens.

ideas.name: Learned Boundary Repair Mask
ideas.question: Can a tiny model discover the minimal cross-boundary relay edges from an overcomplete candidate set, rather than being handed the boundary repair program?
ideas.minimum_test: Train a two-layer copy reader with fixed block edges plus learnable candidate cross-block gates, then score exact copy accuracy together with top-k recovery of the true bridge edges.
ideas.falsifier: If learned gates solve the copy task while failing to rank the true bridge edges above decoys, then accuracy alone is not mechanism evidence and learned repair must be demoted.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Only 16-token synthetic sequences and a dozen candidate edges are needed; CPU PyTorch is enough.

ideas.name: Tiny Route/Gain Trained Readout
ideas.question: Does route/gain decoupling survive a constrained trained readout, or can importance-in-route scoring replace explicit value gain?
ideas.minimum_test: Train route-only, importance-in-route, gain-decoupled and hybrid readouts on weak-source/high-distractor regimes with fixed one-hot values.
ideas.falsifier: If explicit gain is never useful outside contrived regimes and importance-in-route dominates, keep route/gain decoupling as a diagnostic guard rather than a core architecture candidate.
ideas.why_scale_fits: A tiny differentiable readout isolates selection and transmission without needing a transformer stack.

ideas.name: Trained Mechanism Guard Report
ideas.question: Are trained tiny probes carrying the same exactness, sparsity, routing/gain and deployment guard fields as symbolic probes?
ideas.minimum_test: Scan current trained artifacts for primary metrics and mechanism guard fields; require exactness/reachability/route-gain/sparsity evidence before promotion.
ideas.falsifier: If the report only summarizes without changing promotion choices, merge it into trained escalation reporting.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Audit work is cheap and prevents trained toy accuracy from becoming a new source of overclaiming.

ideas.name: Post-Training Sparse Bridge Compilation
ideas.question: Can a dense candidate-bridge model be sparsified after training into a deployable hard sparse mask without losing exact-copy performance?
ideas.minimum_test: Train candidate-edge boundary copy model, freeze core weights, learn only edge priors under exact-copy plus sparsity pressure, then deploy via hard top-k / threshold / hard fine-tune compilers.
ideas.falsifier: If soft post-trained gates solve but no hard compiler recovers exact copy with the correct bridge edges, post-training sparsity is only an interpretability hint, not a deployable sparse program.
ideas.why_scale_fits: The entire problem uses 16-token sequences, 12 candidate edges, and CPU PyTorch; it is ideal for trained-tiny escalation.

ideas.name: Sparse Gate Compiler Frontier
ideas.question: Which hard compiler should turn continuous gate scores into sparse connectivity: threshold, top-k, validation-HPO, uncertainty band, or gap-knee?
ideas.minimum_test: Generate calibrated, shrunken, false-spike, ambiguous and overactive score regimes; compare compiler policies on exact reachability, selected-edge cost, calibration error, rank quality and regret.
ideas.falsifier: If one compiler dominates every regime, the gate-compilation problem is simpler than expected; if all compilers fail shrunken rank-good cases, soft gates are not actionable without calibration.
ideas.why_scale_fits: A C++ score-distribution wind tunnel can sweep thousands of regimes instantly and gives a hardened companion to the trained bridge task.

ideas.name: Hard Gate Compilation Audit
ideas.question: Do sparse/gate/bridge/routing probes explicitly distinguish soft training, hard deployment, exactness, and selected-edge cost?
ideas.minimum_test: Scan current artifacts for hard-top-k accuracy, threshold accuracy, deployment gap, edge F1, calibration/rank quality, target miss and selected-edge cost.
ideas.falsifier: If the audit only counts fields but does not change promotion decisions, merge it into trained mechanism guard reporting.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Audit is cheap and prevents soft-gate accuracy from being promoted as a hard sparse mechanism.

ideas.name: Annealed Hard Bridge Gate Training
ideas.question: Can annealed sparse gate training turn a soft bridge ranking into a hard deployable sparse program without relying on post-hoc probability thresholds?
ideas.minimum_test: Train dense candidate boundary copy, freeze core weights, anneal edge-gate temperature and sparsity pressure, then deploy hard top-k and threshold masks with exact-copy and edge-F1 guards.
ideas.falsifier: If annealed gates solve softly but hard top-k or hard threshold loses exact copy, annealing does not repair the compile gap.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Sixteen tokens, twelve candidate bridge edges, and CPU PyTorch are enough to expose soft/hard deployment gaps.

ideas.name: Blockwise GQA Index Branch Wind Tunnel
ideas.question: When does a MiniMax/MSA-style per-GQA-group block index branch beat dense, local-only, and shared-index sparse attention under exactness and selector-cost guards?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ block-selection simulator with local block, shared index, per-group index, boundary-anchor index, dense, and token oracle across local, boundary, far-needle, group-specific, off-phase, distractor, and smooth regimes.
ideas.falsifier: If per-group block indexing wins only by ignoring selector cost or fails exact-copy/needle regimes, block index branches should remain P1 until trained evidence exists.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Block-level selection is discrete and can be exhaustively stress-tested with thousands of tiny synthetic cases in C++.

ideas.name: GVR Exact Top-K Temporal Selector Toy
ideas.question: Can temporal correlation make exact top-k selection cheaper without approximate misses, and where does drift force fallback?
ideas.minimum_test: C++ stream of sparse-attention index scores; compare radix exact baseline, GVR with verification/fallback, aggressive no-fallback GVR, calibrated threshold, and previous-top-k reuse.
ideas.falsifier: If GVR only wins by becoming approximate or by falling back so often that cost matches baseline, temporal top-k should be treated as systems-only until better score models exist.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Top-k selector cost and exactness can be tested without training a model; this is a pure algorithmic kernel toy.

ideas.name: Hybrid Mask Compiler Frontier
ideas.question: Do hybrid Top-k/Top-p/threshold compilers beat single-rule sparse mask compilation under uniform, skewed, and false-spike attention rows?
ideas.minimum_test: Extend gate compiler frontier with top-p mass caps, hybrid top-k/top-p, compensated thresholding, and validation-chosen thresholds.
ideas.falsifier: If hybrid compilers only win after oracle validation cost is ignored, keep them as score filters rather than architecture mechanisms.
ideas.why_scale_fits: Mask compilation is a small sorted-vector problem; no large model is needed to expose failure modes.

ideas.name: Sparse Index Compiler Audit
ideas.question: Do hard-gate, block-index, and temporal top-k probes all report exactness plus realized selector/block cost in one place?
ideas.minimum_test: Create a sparse index compiler report that scans bridge/gate compiler, block index branch, and GVR artifacts for compile, exactness, block, temporal, and cost readiness.
ideas.falsifier: If the report does not affect promotion priorities, merge it into hard gate compilation report.
ideas.why_scale_fits: The audit is cheap but prevents a sparse mechanism from being promoted on accuracy while hiding top-k or block-routing overhead.
